get.summary: The passkeys of whoever asks.

post.summary:
Keeps a passkey that the browser has just had made with the challenge
`begin` handed out.

409.description: The challenge is no longer out, the key is here already, or there are no passkeys where this was asked from.

422.description: What the device answered does not hold.

post.summary:
Begins making a passkey: checks the account's password, and answers with
what the browser is to ask its device for. The challenge counts for five
minutes, and once.

403.description: The password is wrong.

409.description: There are no passkeys where this was asked from, or the account has as many as it can.

delete.summary:
Removes one of the passkeys of whoever asks. The device goes on holding
its half, which opens nothing here any more.

204.description: It is gone.

404.description: The account has no such passkey.

post.summary:
Changes the password of whoever asks. Every other session of the account
ends; the one that asked goes on.

204.description: The account has the new password.

403.description: The current password is wrong.

422.description: The new password will not do.

get.summary:
Whether the account signed in here has a second step, and how many
recovery codes it has left.

post.summary:
Begins giving the account a second step: makes a secret for an
authenticator app. Nothing changes until a code from that app has been
typed back, which shows the app has it.

409.description: The account has a second step already.

post.summary:
Turns the second step on, given a code from the app that was just set up.
The answer is the account's recovery codes, which are not shown again.

409.description: No app is being set up.

422.description: The code is not the app's.

post.summary: Turns the second step of the account that asks off, given its password.

204.description: The account signs in with its password alone.

403.description: The password is wrong.

get.summary:
What was done through the panel, the newest first, a hundred lines at a
time. The one request the Activity page needs.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Only what was done to the server with this id.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Only what the account with this id did.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only what is older than the line with this id: for the page after the first.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

get.summary: The catalogue as it was last fetched. Empty until it has been.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary:
Fetches the catalogue afresh from where the eggs are published, and keeps
it. A collection that could not be listed leaves the whole as it was.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: The catalogue could not be fetched.

get.summary:
Every VPS, how the tunnel to each is doing, and every port they forward.
The one request the Network page needs, and the one the sidebar's mark
asks again.

post.summary:
Starts connecting a VPS: makes the keys of a tunnel to it and answers with
the one command to run there. The command counts for a quarter of an hour.
Core dials the VPS from now until then, and the tunnel is up within a few
seconds of the command being run; asking for the VPSes again shows it.
post.description:
A VPS that was being connected and is not yet is given up for this one.
Those that are connected stay as they are.

201.description: The command is ready, and the VPS is awaited.

409.description: That VPS is connected already, or there is no room for one more.

422.description: The address, the name or the port will not do.

get.summary:
What passes through each VPS's tunnel now, and has for the last few
minutes: what the Network page draws. Home counts it, at its own end of
each tunnel, so nothing is asked of a VPS for it.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary: Changes what a VPS is called.

422.description: The name will not do.

delete.summary:
Forgets a VPS and takes home's end of the tunnel to it down. The servers
that were reached through it are reached through the best of the VPSes
that are left, or on the home network only if none is. The VPS keeps its
Gate program until `homewarp-gate leave` is run there.

204.description: The VPS is not connected any more.

post.summary:
Finds out again whether servers behind a VPS see their players' own
addresses, and puts its Gate in the mode that works. It takes a few
seconds, during which new connections through it may be turned away.

409.description: The VPS is not connected, or it cannot be reached.

get.summary: The guard on the VPS itself, and what is listening there.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: No VPS is connected, or its Gate cannot be reached.

put.summary:
Hardens the VPS: from now on, what arrives at the VPS itself from the
internet is dropped, but for what is listening there at this moment, and
new SSH connections from one address are held to a few a minute. What is
forwarded to servers is not touched.
put.description:
It is on trial. In a minute the VPS undoes it by itself, unless it has been
kept by then.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: No VPS is connected, or its Gate cannot be reached or would not.

delete.summary: Takes the guard away, kept or on trial.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: No VPS is connected, or its Gate cannot be reached.

post.summary:
Keeps a guard that is on trial. The VPS writes it down, and comes back
with it after a restart.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: There is no guard to keep: its minute was over. Or the Gate cannot be reached.

post.summary:
Signs in with a passkey: the device signed the challenge, and checked who
was holding it, so neither a password nor a code is asked for.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

401.description: The passkey did not sign in.

409.description: There are no passkeys where this was asked from.

post.summary:
Begins a sign-in with a passkey: answers with a challenge for the device
to sign. Nobody is named: the device says which key it has.

409.description: There are no passkeys where this was asked from.

204.description: Signed out.

get.summary:
The panel's way in from the internet: its name, its certificate, and how
the asking for one stands.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Gives the panel a name, or takes its name away. With a name, a connected
VPS forwards the panel's port home, and a certificate for the name is
asked for at once and kept renewed; asking for the panel again shows how
that stands. Without one the port is forwarded no more.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: This Homewarp has no door for TLS.

422.description: That is not a name, or the authority's terms were not agreed to.

post.summary:
Asks for the certificate again now, without waiting out the hour that
follows an asking that failed.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: The panel has no name.

get.summary: Every server, by name. The one request the Servers page needs.

post.summary:
Makes a server from a template, then installs and starts it. The answer
comes at once; the install goes on, and the server's console shows it.

409.description: The name or the port belongs to another server.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

get.summary:
One server, with its state and the end of its console. A page that stays
open asks again to follow both.

put.summary:
Changes what a server is made of. It has to be stopped first, and what was
changed counts from its next start.

409.description: The server is running, or the name or the port belongs to another.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

delete.summary: Removes a server that is not running, with its files.

204.description: The server and its files are gone.

409.description: The server is running.

get.summary:
A server's backups, the newest first, and how many are kept. The one
request the Backups tab needs.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

post.summary:
Begins a backup of everything in a server's files. The answer comes at
once, with the backup as it stands; asking for the backups again shows how
it went. A server that runs meanwhile goes on running.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

409.description: A backup of it is being made already.

422.description: The name will not do.

put.summary:
Says how many finished backups of a server are kept. It counts from the
next backup that is done: none goes because of this alone.

204.description: That many are kept from now on.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

422.description: It is not a number from 1 to 20.

delete.summary: Deletes a backup. It cannot be brought back.

204.description: The backup is gone.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The backup is still being made.

post.summary:
Copies a finished backup to the store elsewhere: one that was made before
there was a store, or whose copy did not arrive. The answer comes at once,
and asking for the backups again shows how it went.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: There is no store, the backup was not finished, or it is being copied already.

get.summary: A backup's file as it is: a tar packed with Zstandard, for the browser to save.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The backup was not finished.

post.summary:
Makes a server's files what a backup says they were: everything in them
now goes, and the backup is unpacked in their place. The server has to be
stopped. The answer comes at once; the server shows as being restored
until it is done, and its console says how it went.

202.description: The backup is being put back.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such backup.

409.description: The server is running, or the backup was not finished.

post.summary: Types one line into the console of a server that is starting or running.

204.description: The line is on its way to the server.

409.description: The server is not running.

422.description: That is not one line.

get.summary: What is in one folder of a server's files: folders first, then by name.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such folder.

422.description: That is not a folder.

get.summary:
A file's text, for the editor. A file that is not text, or is longer than
four megabytes, is refused: those are for downloading.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

422.description: That is not a file of text, or it is too long.

put.summary:
Writes a file: an upload, or what the editor saves. The body is the file as
it is. It takes the place of a file that is there by that name, and only
once all of it has arrived; the folders it sits in are made if they are not there.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

204.description: The file is there.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

409.description: The disk has no room for it.

422.description: That is no path for a file, or the upload was cut off.

get.summary: A file as it is, to be saved by the browser and never shown by it.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A path from the top of the server's files. Empty, or left out, is the top itself.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

422.description: That is not a file.

post.summary: Makes a folder.

204.description: The folder is there.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

409.description: Something by that name is there already.

422.description: That is no path for a folder.

post.summary:
Moves a file or a folder, which is also how it is given another name.
Never onto something that is there already.

204.description: It is where it was asked to be.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or nothing at `from`.

409.description: Something is at `to` already.

422.description: One of the two is no path in the server's files.

post.summary:
Packs files and folders into one gzipped tar, in the folder they are in.
The answer comes when it is done, which for a world takes a while.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or one of the names is not there.

409.description: The disk has no room for it.

422.description: Nothing was named, or one of the names is not one.

post.summary:
Deletes files, and folders with all that is in them. They cannot be
brought back. It stops at the first that cannot be deleted.

204.description: They are gone.

403.description: A path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or one of them is not there.

422.description: One of them is no path in the server's files.

post.summary:
Unpacks a zip, a tar or a gzipped tar into the folder it is in, over what is
there by the same names. The answer comes when it is done.

403.description: The path leads out of the server's files.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such file.

409.description: The disk has no room for what is in it.

422.description: That is not an archive Homewarp can read.

get.summary:
How much of the disk a server's files take, and how much of it is left.
Every file is asked, so a page should not wait for this before it paints.

Mods or plugins on Modrinth for what this server runs: by what was typed,
or the most downloaded where nothing was. Core asks Modrinth; the page
does not.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to look for. With none, the most downloaded are answered.

parameters.name: loader
parameters.description:
What loads it on this server: paper, purpur, folia, spigot, bukkit,
velocity, bungeecord, waterfall, fabric, quilt, forge or neoforge.

parameters.name: game
parameters.description: The version of Minecraft the server runs, such as 1.21.1. Left out, any.

403.description: The account has not been let write this server's files.

409.description: Modrinth could not be asked, or did not answer as expected.

422.description: The loader or the version is not one.

post.summary:
Fetches a release's file from Modrinth and puts it in the folder this
server's loader reads: `plugins` or `mods`. It is written only once its
checksum is the one Modrinth gives for it, and is loaded when the server
next starts. What the release needs beside itself is not installed with it.

403.description: The account has not been let write this server's files.

409.description: The file could not be fetched, was not the file Modrinth describes, or there is no room for it.

422.description: The release or the loader is not one, or the release is not for that loader.

get.summary: The newest releases of one project for what this server runs.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to look for. With none, the most downloaded are answered.

parameters.name: loader
parameters.description:
What loads it on this server: paper, purpur, folia, spigot, bukkit,
velocity, bungeecord, waterfall, fabric, quilt, forge or neoforge.

parameters.name: game
parameters.description: The version of Minecraft the server runs, such as 1.21.1. Left out, any.

403.description: The account has not been let write this server's files.

409.description: Modrinth could not be asked, or did not answer as expected.

422.description: The project, the loader or the version is not one.

post.summary:
Starts, stops or kills a server, or installs one again whose install failed.
The answer comes once the request is on its way, not once it is carried out.

204.description: The server has been asked.

409.description: The state the server is in rules that out.

get.summary: A server's schedules, by name. The one request the Schedules tab needs.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

post.summary: Makes a schedule.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

409.description: The server has as many schedules as it may.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

put.summary: Changes a schedule. When it runs next is worked out afresh.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

422.description: Something asked for will not do.

204.description: The schedule is gone.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

post.summary:
Sets a schedule off now, whatever its times and whether or not it is
enabled. The answer comes at once; the schedule says what the run came to.

403.description: The account has not been let do this.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such schedule.

get.summary:
The accounts that have been let into a server, by name. The owner is not
among them: it is in every server.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Lets an account into a server, or changes what it may do there. With no
permission named it may look, and no more.

204.description: The account may do what was named, and no more.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

404.description: There is no such server, or no such account.

422.description: It is the owner's account.

delete.summary: Takes an account out of a server. To that account the server is then not there.

204.description: The account is out of the server.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

404.description: That account was not in that server.

get.summary:
Who is signed in, and whether setup is still to do. The one request a page
needs before it can paint.

What is set. The one request the owner's part of the Settings page needs
beside the accounts.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Changes what is set, and leaves what is not named as it is. Where servers
look names up counts from each server's next start: one that is running
goes on asking where it asked. The limit on new connections counts as soon
as the Gate is told, which is at once.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

422.description: A resolver is not an address servers can reach, or the limit is not one that can be set.

put.summary:
Has every backup that is made from now on copied to a store elsewhere: a
bucket that is spoken to as Amazon's S3 is. The store is tried first, with
a few bytes written and taken away again, and is kept only if it took
them: a store that is thought to hold copies and holds none is worse than
none. The key's secret is kept and not given back.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: The store could not be reached, or would not be written to.

422.description: Something given is not what a store's settings look like.

delete.summary: Has backups copied nowhere from now on. What is in the store stays there.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary: Creates the first account and signs it in. Works once.

200.description: The account exists and is signed in.

403.description: The setup code is wrong.

409.description: There is an account already.

422.description: The username or password will not do.

get.summary: Every template, by name. The one request the Templates page needs.

post.summary: Reads an egg and keeps it as a template.

409.description: There is a template of that name already.

422.description: This is not an egg Homewarp can read.

post.summary:
Fetches an egg's text from the address it is published at, for its owner
to read and then import. Nothing is imported by this.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

422.description: That address is not one eggs are fetched from, or nothing could be fetched from it.

204.description: The template is gone.

409.description: A server is made from it.

get.summary:
Which version runs, whether a newer one is out, and whether this Homewarp
can put it in place itself. The one request the Updates page needs.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

put.summary:
Says which releases this Homewarp takes: only what has been released, or
what is being tried before it is as well.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary: Looks for a newer release now, where Homewarp otherwise looks every few hours.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary:
Puts the newest release of this Homewarp's channel in place of the one
that runs. The answer comes at once; the update goes on, and asking how it
stands shows it. Homewarp stops answering for a moment near the end, and
answers again as the new version, or as the old one if the new one did not
start. Servers that are running go on running all the while.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: There is nothing newer, an update is being made already, or this Homewarp cannot replace itself.

get.summary: Every account, the owner's first. The one request the Users page needs.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary: Makes an account. It can sign in at once, and sees no server until it is let into one.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: There is an account by that name already.

422.description: The username or password will not do.

delete.summary: Removes an account, signs it out everywhere and takes it out of every server.

204.description: The account is gone.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

409.description: It is the owner's account.

put.summary:
Gives an account another password, for whoever has forgotten theirs. The
account is signed out wherever it was signed in.

204.description: The account has the new password.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

422.description: The password will not do.

delete.summary:
Turns another account's second step off: for whoever has lost both their
app and their recovery codes.

204.description: The account signs in with its password alone.

403.description: The account asking is not the owner's.

get.summary:
The webhooks, by name, and everything one can be told of. The one request
the Webhooks page needs.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary:
Has this Homewarp tell an address what happens to it: every line of the
Activity page, or the ones that are named. The address is one that takes a
message as JSON.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: There are as many webhooks as there may be.

422.description: That is not an address that can be told, or nothing it could be told of.

put.summary:
Changes a webhook: its name, what it is told of and, where one is given,
its address. How the last thing it was sent went is forgotten with the
address it was sent to.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

422.description: That is not an address that can be told, or nothing it could be told of.

delete.summary: Has this Homewarp tell an address no more.

204.description: The webhook is gone.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

post.summary:
Sends a webhook a line that says only that it is reached, and waits for
the site to take it.

403.description: The account is not the owner's.

409.description: The site did not take it.

Account.description: An account, as the owner sees it among the others.

created_at.description: When it was made, in Unix seconds.

servers.description: How many servers it has been let into. The owner is in all of them, and this says nothing of it.

Activity.description: What passes through the tunnels now, and has for the last few minutes.

every_seconds.description: How many seconds lie between one sample and the next.

most.description: How many samples the whole of it is.

action.description: What was done, as a name such as `server.start` or `files.remove`.

detail.description: What it was done with: a path, a name, a command.

server.description: That server's name at the time.

server_id.description: The server it was done to, if it was done to one.

user_id.description: Whose account did it. None once that account has been removed.

username.description: That account's name at the time.

created_at.description: When it was begun, in Unix seconds.

problem.description: Why it failed, if it did.

size_bytes.description: How long the file is. Nothing until it is done.

oneOf.description:
Where its copy in the store elsewhere stands. Nothing where no copy
was asked for: there was no store when it was made.

stored_problem.description: Why it was not copied, if it was not.

Backups.description: A server's backups, and how many of them are kept.

kept.description: When one more is done, the oldest beyond this many go.

store.description: Whether there is a store elsewhere that backups are copied to.

BeginPasskey.description: What making a passkey begins with.

password.description:
The account's password: a passkey is another way in, and whoever adds
one has to be the account's owner and not only someone at its browser.

Catalogue.description: The catalogue as it was last fetched.

fetched_at.description: When, in Unix seconds. Nothing if it never was.

CatalogueEgg.description: One egg there is to be had.

kind.description: The collection it is in: `minecraft`, `games-steamcmd` and so on.

name.description: What it is called, as its file's name has it.

url.description: Where its text is fetched from.

CertificateView.description: The certificate the panel is served with.

authority.description: Who issued it: the machine of the authority's directory.

issued_at.description:
When it was issued, when it ends and when a newer one is asked for, in
Unix seconds.

command.description: One line, as it would be typed into the server's console.

Delivery.description: How the last thing a webhook was sent went.

problem.description: Why the site did not take it. Nothing if it did.

free_bytes.description: What is left on the disk they are on.

used_bytes.description: What the server's files take of the disk.

EggAddress.description: Where an egg is to be fetched from.

url.description: An address that begins with `https://`, by a name, on the usual port.

oneOf.description:
Where things stand. It comes first, and again for a page that has
fallen too far behind to be caught up line by line.

first.description: The number of the first of `lines`.

oneOf.description: One more line of the console.
About once a second while the server runs.

Who is on it, where the server says: a few times a minute while it
runs, and nothing once it does not.

Event.description: What a page that follows a server is sent, over its socket.

ExtraPort.description: A further port of a server: voice chat, say, or the port it is queried on.

FetchedEgg.description: An egg's text, as it was fetched. Nothing has been done with it.

modified.description: When it was last changed, in Unix seconds.

size.description: In bytes. Nothing for what is not a file.

path.description: Where the new folder goes. The folders it sits in are made with it.

ForwardedPort.description: A port of a server, which the Gate of its VPS forwards.

gate_id.description:
The VPS the server is reached through. None while it is reached on the
home network only.

traffic_bytes.description:
What that VPS's Gate counted through it in the last day, both ways
together. Nothing where no Gate has counted.

slug.description: The name it has in its address there: modrinth.com/project/<slug>.

GateActivity.description: What passed through one VPS's tunnel, a look at a time.

samples.description:
The newest last. Fewer than the whole of it for a tunnel that has not
been up that long.

GateSettings.description: What can be changed of a VPS that is connected.

GateView.description: A VPS, and how the tunnel to it is doing.

address.description: The VPS's public address: what players type.

command.description:
While the VPS is awaited: what to run on it, as root. Where this
Homewarp knows where its releases are, the command fetches the Gate
first; otherwise it takes the Gate to be on the VPS already.

expires_at.description: When that command stops counting, in Unix seconds.

handshake_age_seconds.description: How long ago the Gate last heard from home over the tunnel.

latency_ms.description: How long the way to the Gate and back takes, in milliseconds.

load_percent.description:
How busy the VPS is: 100 is every processor it has in use. Nothing
from a Gate that does not say.

name.description: What its owner calls it. Its address, until it is called something.

note.description: What the check of that found, where it needs saying.

player_addresses.description: Whether servers see their players' own addresses.

problem.description: Why the Gate could not be reached, when it could not.

reachable.description: Whether the Gate answered through the tunnel when it was last asked.

received_bytes_per_second.description:
What passes through its tunnel in a second, now: from players to
servers, and from servers to players.

servers.description: How many servers are reached through it.

traffic_bytes.description:
What its Gate counted through the ports of servers in the last day,
both ways together.

version.description: The version of the Gate program on the VPS.

permissions.description: What the account may do with the server beyond looking at it. None is looking only.

Happening.description: One thing that is written down, and so can be told.

by_itself.description: Whether it happens with nobody at the panel.

egg.description: The egg as a panel exports it: JSON or YAML.

InstallUpdate.description: What an update is asked with.

servers.description:
Back every server up first, as its Backups tab does, and go on only
once every backup is made. Homewarp's own database is copied either
way: it is what is put back if the new version does not start.

path.description: The file, from the top of the server's files.

at.description: When that was found out, in Unix seconds.

detail.description:
What went wrong, where something did: the end of what was written
down while it was tried.

ok.description: Whether that version is the one that runs now.

code.description:
The code of the second step, for an account that has one: from its
authenticator app, or one of its recovery codes.

MakeOptions.description: What a browser is asked to make a passkey with.

challenge.description: What the device is to sign, in the base64 that uses neither `+` nor `/`.

exclude.description:
The keys the account has here already, by what their devices call
them, so that a device is not given a second.

rp_id.description: The name the key is bound to.

user_handle.description: What the device files the key under: the account, in that base64.

to.description: Where it goes, its own name included: the same folder for a new name.

Network.description: Every VPS, and every port players reach a server by.

gates.description: The VPSes, the first that was connected first.

oneOf.description:
Which of them a server is best reached through, where more than
nothing is known. A new server is reached through it unless another
is asked for.

password.description: What it signs in with at first. Whoever it is for can change it.

name.description: What to call it. Something is made up if nothing is given.

NewGate.description: What it takes to start connecting a VPS.

address.description: The VPS's public IPv4 address, or a name for it.

name.description: What to call it. Its address, if nothing is given.

wg_port.description: The UDP port its WireGuard is to listen on. 51820 if none is given.

NewPasskey.description: A passkey a browser has just had made.

client_data.description:
What the browser says it was asked, and what the device answered, each
in the base64 that uses neither `+` nor `/`.

current.description: The password as it is now.

password.description: The one to have from now on.

folder.description: The folder the archive is made in.

names.description: What goes into it: names in that folder.

name.description: The archive's name, in the folder it was asked for in.

agreed.description:
That the owner agrees to the terms of the authority certificates are
asked of. Asked for with a name.

name.description:
The name the panel is to be reached by, which has to lead to the VPS
already. Nothing takes the panel off the internet again.

PanelState.description: Where the panel stands with the internet.

PanelView.description: The panel's way in from the internet.

address.description: Where the panel is, once it has a certificate for its name.

answers.description:
The directory a web server on the VPS has to serve at
`/.well-known/acme-challenge/` for the name, where the VPS has one on
port 80. Nothing where the Gate serves the answers itself.

available.description:
Whether this Homewarp can be reached by a name at all: whether it was
started with a door for TLS.

caa.description:
A DNS record for the name, of type CAA, that has the authority give a
certificate for it to this Homewarp and to nobody else: not to
whoever has the VPS, which is where the name leads. Nothing where the
authority is not known to honour such a record.

name.description: The name it has been given.

port.description: The port the panel is reached on by its name, on the VPS and at home alike.

problem.description: Why the last asking for a certificate failed, if it did.

PasskeySignIn.description: A sign-in made with a passkey.

id.description: What the device calls the key that signed.

PasskeyView.description: A passkey, as its owner sees it.

created_at.description: In Unix seconds, as every time here.

last_used_at.description: When it last signed in. Nothing if it never has.

available.description: Whether one can be made, or used, where this was asked from.

Permission.description: Something an account may be let do with a server, beyond looking at it.

PlayerAddresses.description: Whether servers see their players' own addresses, as the self-probe found it.

Players.description: Who is on a server, as it says itself to anyone who asks.

max.description: How many it lets on at once.

names.description: Some of their names. A server gives a sample, and a full one not even that.

PortProtocol.description: Which protocols a port is published for at home and forwarded for by the Gate.

Ports.description: Ports, by the two kinds there are.

Power.description: What a person can ask of a server.

ProblemBody.description: The body of every error response.

code_required.description: True when what is missing is the code of the second step of a sign-in.

error.description: A sentence fit to show to the person using the panel.

Rate.description: What passed through a tunnel in a second: to the servers, and from them.

received.description: From players to servers, in bytes.

sent.description: From servers to players, in bytes.

Recommended.description: The VPS a server is best reached through, and what speaks for it.

why.description: As a line under the choice: "23 ms from home, 12 % busy, 1 server on it".

RecoveryCodes.description:
The codes that sign an account in when its app is lost. Each works once,
and they are shown this one time.

games.description: The versions of Minecraft it is for, oldest first.

number.description: The version its authors gave it.

requires.description: How many other projects it needs, which are not installed with it.

paths.description: Files, and folders with all that is in them.

cron.description: When it runs, as cron writes it: minute, hour, day, month, weekday.

last_result.description: What the last run came to, in a sentence.

next_run_at.description: When it runs next, in Unix seconds. Never, while it is not enabled.

only_running.description: Whether a time at which the server is not running is passed over.

utc_offset.description: The clock those are read on: minutes east of UTC.
The clock of whoever sets it: minutes east of UTC.

Server.description: A server in full, with the end of its console.

console.description: The last lines of its console: the install first, then what the server prints.

cpu_percent.description: 100 is one core. 0 is no limit.

created_at.description: When it was made, in Unix seconds.

eula.description: Whether the game's EULA was agreed to for it.

gate_id.description:
The VPS it is reached through, whose address is the one players type.
None while no VPS is connected: it is then reached at home only.

mods.description: Whether it is one of Minecraft's, which mods or plugins can be found for.

permissions.description: What the account that asks may do with it, beyond looking at it.

oneOf.description: Who is on it, for a running server that says.

port.description: Where players reach it, on the home machine and on a connected VPS.

protocol.description: Which protocols that port is open for.

says_offline.description: Whether players are told that it is offline while it is stopped.

sleep_minutes.description:
How many minutes it may run with nobody on it before it is put to
sleep, to be woken when a player joins. 0 is never.

template.description: The name of the template it was made from.

variables.description: The value of each of the template's variables, by the name the server sees.

ServerSettings.description: What a server is made of that can still be changed once it is made.

cpu_percent.description: 100 is one core. Nothing, or 0, is no limit.

eula.description: Whoever asks agrees to the EULA of the game, for a game that has one.

gate_id.description:
The VPS to reach it through, of those that are connected. With none
named, a new server takes the one Homewarp recommends, and a server
that is changed keeps the one it has.

image.description: One of the template's images. Its first, if none is named.

port.description: Published on the home machine, and forwarded by a connected VPS.

ports.description: Further ports, each published and forwarded as the first is.

protocol.description: Which protocols that port is open for. Both, if none is named.

says_offline.description:
While it is stopped, have something small listen on its port and tell
the game's list, and a player who joins, that it is offline. For a
server of Minecraft's; it is nothing to any other.

sleep_minutes.description:
Put to sleep after this many minutes with nobody on it, and woken when
a player joins. Nothing, or 0, is never. It needs a server that says
who is on it, which is one of Minecraft's.

variables.description:
Values for the template's variables, by the name the server sees. One
that is not given takes the template's default.

ServerSummary.description: A server as the Servers page shows it.

gate_id.description: The VPS it is reached through. None while it is reached at home only.

oneOf.description: Who is on it, for a running server that says.

port.description: Where players reach it on the home machine.

template.description: The name of the template it was made from.

ServerUser.description: An account that has been let into a server.

permissions.description: What it may do there beyond looking.

Session.description: Everything the web interface needs to decide what to show first.

setup_required.description: True until the first account has been created.

sftp_port.description: The port SFTP is reached on at this machine, where it is served.

oneOf.description: Who is signed in, if anyone.

new_connections.description:
How many new connections a second a connected VPS lets one address on
the internet open to the servers, with twice as many at once. More
are dropped at the VPS, so that one address cannot crowd the rest out.

resolvers.description:
Where servers look names up: one to three IPv4 addresses on the
internet. A change counts from each server's next start.

oneOf.description: Where backups are copied to beside where they are kept. Nothing if nowhere.

SettingsChange.description: What is to be changed. What is not named is left as it is.

code.description: The code Homewarp wrote to its log when it started.

SignInOptions.description: What a browser is asked to sign in with.

Step.description: Where an update that is being made stands.

StoreChange.description: A store for backups: a bucket that is spoken to as Amazon's S3 is.

endpoint.description:
Where it is: `https://s3.example.com`, or `http://192.168.1.20:9000`
for one at home.

key_id.description: The key that may write to the bucket, and its secret.

prefix.description: A folder in the bucket to keep to. Left out, none.

region.description: Its region. `us-east-1` if none is given, which most stores take.

StoreView.description:
The store elsewhere, as the page is told of it: without its key's secret,
which is kept and not given back.

prefix.description: The folder in the bucket. Empty for none.

Stored.description: Where a backup's copy in the store elsewhere stands.

Task.description: One thing a schedule does. They are done in the order they are given in.

command.description: The line to type, for a command. Nothing for anything else.

wait_seconds.description:
How long to wait before it, in seconds: after the task before it, or
after the time came for the first.

Template.description: A template in full: everything Homewarp will do on its word.

config_files.description: The files patched in a server's directory before every start.

created_at.description: When it was imported, in Unix seconds.

done.description: A server has started once its console prints any of these.

images.description: The first is the one a new server runs in unless another is picked.

oneOf.description: What runs once, before a server's first start. Not every template has it.

startup.description: The command that starts a server, with `{{NAME}}` where a variable goes.

TemplateStop.description: How a server is asked to shut down.

value.description: The command typed into the console, or the name of the signal sent.

TemplateSummary.description: A template as the gallery shows it.

image.description: The image a new server runs in unless another is picked.

env.description: The environment variable the server sees.

rules.description: Laravel-style validation rules, one per entry.

TwoSteps.description: Whether the account that asks has a second step to its sign-in.

recovery_codes.description: How many of its recovery codes have not been used.

TwoStepsSetup.description: What an authenticator app is given to make the codes of an account.

secret.description: The secret, to type into the app.

uri.description: The same as a link, which an app on this device opens.

path.description: A zip, a tar or a gzipped tar. It is unpacked into the folder it is in.

skipped.description:
How many entries were left out: those that would have gone outside the
server's files, and what is neither a file, a folder nor a link.

UpdateSettings.description: What can be set about updates.

UpdateView.description: What there is to know about updates.

available.description: Whether that is newer than what is running.

by_hand.description: Why it cannot, where it cannot.

checked_at.description: When it last looked for a newer one, in Unix seconds.

gate_line.description:
The line that puts this release's Gate in place of an older one, run
as root on a VPS.

installs.description: Whether this Homewarp can put a newer version in place of itself.

line.description:
The line that installs the newest release by hand, on the machine
Homewarp runs on. Nothing where it is not known where releases are.

newest.description: The newest release for its channel, where the list of them could be read.

problem.description: Why the list could not be read, or why the last update could not be begun.

oneOf.description: An update that is being made now.

Updating.description: An update that is being made.

Usage.description: How much of the machine a running server is using.

cpu_percent.description: Of one core: 150 is a core and a half.

memory_limit_bytes.description: The most it may use before it is stopped.

received_bytes_per_second.description:
What arrives for it over the network in a second, and what it sends:
players for the most part, and whatever else it talks to.

owner.description:
The account made at setup. It may do everything; any other account
only what it has been let do, with the servers it has been let into.

VpsGuard.description: The guard on the VPS itself.

dropped.description: How many packets the guard has dropped since it was put in place.

listening.description:
What is listening on the VPS now, where the internet can reach it.
This is what hardening would keep open.

open.description: What it keeps open on the VPS itself. Nothing where there is no guard.

seconds_left.description: On trial: how many seconds are left before it is undone by itself.

shut.description:
What is listening now and is shut all the same: it began to listen
after the guard was put in place.

loader.description: What loads it on this server, which says which folder it goes in.

events.description: What to tell it of, where that is not everything.

everything.description: Every line of the Activity page.

url.description:
An address that takes a message as JSON, as a Discord or a Slack
webhook does: `https`, by a name, on the internet. Left out or empty
for a webhook that is there already, it stays the address it has.

WebhookView.description:
A webhook, as the page is told of it: its address is a secret of the
site's making, and is not given back whole.

address.description: The site, and the last few characters of the address.

events.description:
What it is told of, where that is not everything: names such as
`server.crash`, in the order they are listed in.

everything.description: Whether it is told of every line of the Activity page.

oneOf.description: How what it was last sent went, once it has been sent something.

events.description: Everything a webhook can be told of.
